title: Continuation Failure Object and Undefined Composition
purpose: Define what happens when continuation composition, reduction, or typed transition fails admissibility or domain guards.
core_claim: Continuation failure is a marked diagnostic state, not a lawful continuation object.

canonical_claims.statement: Failed composition does not produce a continuation object.
Continuation failure is a marked diagnostic state, not an RT condition.
Typed-domain failure, endpoint mismatch, admissibility failure, or residue-propagation failure may produce ⊥C.
⊥C must not be reduced into NF(C).

formal_objects.name: Continuation Failure
formal_objects.definition: The marked failure state produced when a proposed continuation cannot be admitted as a lawful continuation object.

failure_rules.name: Type Failure
failure_rules.formal: type(cod(C1)) != type(dom(C2)) and no explicit_transition => Compose(C1,C2) = ⊥C

failure_rules.name: Reduction Failure
failure_rules.formal: WF(C) and not reducible(C) due to guard failure => Reduce(C) = ⊥C

validation_requirements: Register ⊥C as a non-primitive diagnostic failure marker.
Failure is distinct from lawful continuation.
Composition or reduction failure does not produce C(A,C).

next_recommended_patch.title: Continuation Failure Classification and Recovery Boundaries
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Classify continuation failure modes and define the boundary between diagnostic failure and recovery semantics.
